Therefore on Purim one is obligated to become intoxicated until he does not know, for then a person is revealed through his cup: he acts only according to the power implanted within him, with no restraint upon his spirit.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: In the beginning God created. 'Created' (bara) is an expression of strengthening, meaning that initially He reinforced and strengthened the foundations so they could sustain the creation, like a king who builds a storehouse and strengthens the foundations and walls so they can hold whatever he places inside it; and heaven and earth are the foundations of the cosmos, and within the human soul they allude to the heart and the mind; when a person wishes to conduct himself according to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, in order to become a complete creation, he must then fortify and strengthen these two foundational pillars, namely to surrender the intellect…

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Deuteronomy 8:5: ‘Bear in mind that the ETERNAL your God disciplines you just as a man disciplines his son.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Deuteronomy 8:5) to illuminate his exposition here (“And all His exacting scrutiny with the righteous and with the collective seed of Israel is: "as a man chastens his son..." [Deuteronomy 8:5], which stems from mercy, as a father pities his children, like someone...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Wherefore his mercy and lovingkindness were extended unto them while they were still gentiles; (and even after converting, their descendants did not remain beneath the wings of the Shechinah, Hashem's eternal portion being Israel alone whom He brought before Sinai); because Avraham's Chesed was boundless expansion, not yet channeled through the contractions of the Torah; through which unholy dross emerged in Ishmael, the unholy Chesed of the Sitra Achra filled with carnal lusts.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 1:27 (§2)
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: They maintained the consciousness that 'unto Hashem belongs the earth and its fullness,' and on their own part they possess no power to create wealth, only Hashem their God is the One Who gives them power to get wealth (Deuteronomy 8:18); therefore their bread neither mouldered nor broke, remaining as hot at its removal as at its arrangement, because they were intimately close unto Hashem Who is One.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Amos 3:2: ‘You alone have I singled outOf all the families of the earth—That is why I will call you to accountFor all your iniquities.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Amos 3:2) to illuminate his exposition here (“And as it is said (Amos 3:2): "You only have I known... therefore I will visit upon you...", which the Gemara concludes is executed in mercy, as written in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (4a), for yada'ti ("I have...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And through this return in repentance to Hashem, all dedicated unto Him; and this is “behold, I offered my soul before You”— meaning: it was solely for the honor of Your Name, as mentioned. And the sign is: that immediately afterward the ram was “caught in the thicket by his horns”, which signifies awe as noted above, showing that afflictions immediately birthed awe, which is the very purpose for which they arrive.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Genesis, Noach 1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And Hashem said in His heart: I will not again curse the ground anymore for man's sake, etc. And behold, this was the central, quintessential utterance for the entire developmental unfolding of Creation, that they should desire unity and not be separated; for previously, when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Noah: "The end of all flesh has come before Me, etc.", he did not plead for mercy upon his generation; however, afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, placed into the heart of all created beings that they should yearn for unity, like Abraham who beseeched mercy for Sodom, and Moses, even though the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: "And I will…

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Avodah Zarah 4a: ‘And this is the same as that which Rabbi Abba says: What is the meaning of that which is written: “And though I will redeem them, they have spoken lies against Me” (Hosea 7:13)? I said that I would redeem them through taking away their money in this world so that they should merit the World-to-Come, but they have spoken lies against Me, by saying that I am angry and uninterested in them.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Avodah Zarah 4a) to illuminate his exposition here (“And as it is said (Amos 3:2): "You only have I known... therefore I will visit upon you...", which the Gemara concludes is executed in mercy, as written in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (4a), for yada'ti ("I have...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: So that even when Israel "couches and lies down" in descent and lowliness, they remain formidable "as a lion and as a lioness" (Numbers 24:9). And this transcendence is granted purely through divine grace and charity, for in human truth even the most pious cannot escape carnal taint. Therefore "God is angry every day" (Psalms 7:12; Avodah Zarah 4a), for Hashem despises unchaste licentiousness.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 9
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: I will make him a help meet for him. He explained the matter: for such is the will of the Creator, blessed be He, that help and support should flourish for a person from that which opposes him, namely like a disciple to his master, as we find (Bava Metzia 84a) regarding Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish facing Rabbi Yochanan, who would raise twenty-four difficulties against him and he would resolve them with twenty-four solutions, and the teaching was consequently broadened and clarified, and not like Rabbi Elazar who merely told him: 'there is a Baraita that supports you'; for through a person seeing the challenges raised against him, he then fortifies his words…

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Ruth 3:2: ‘Now there is our kinsman Boaz, whose girls you were close to. He will be winnowing barley on the threshing floor tonight.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Ruth 3:2) to illuminate his exposition here (“for yada'ti ("I have known") shares the root of moda ("kinsman/beloved") [Ruth 3:2], meaning love, therefore efkod ("I will visit") means with active visitation and providence, not by withdrawing providence and...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And the sweetening of the bitter in deed and in action was not revealed until Shlomo HaMelech, who knew the sweetening of the tormus — a physical thing that alludes to physical action and deed. And all of Sefer Mishlei is founded on this: “to know chochmah and mussar” — “chochmah” is the clear recognition, as the Sages said [Sanhedrin 7a] on the verse “say to wisdom, you are my sister” (Mishlei 7:4) [kinswoman]’ — a close relative (as in ‘Boaz our kinsman,’ Rus 3:2), that is, keep her ever near you.”
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Kedoshim 11:6
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: He said to him, ‘My son, of this it is written (Ruth, 3:7), ‘she uncovered her feet, and laid down.’ According to the actions of man, thus the soul goes out of her place, and descends below her place. This is like the Shechina, of whom it is written (Yeshayahu, 50:1), “for your transgressions your mother was sent away.”

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Lamentations 1:5: ‘Her enemies are now the masters,Her foes are at ease,Because GOD has afflicted herFor her many transgressions;Her infants have gone into captivityBefore the enemy.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Lamentations 1:5) to illuminate his exposition here (“whereas regarding the Children of Israel it is said: "for Hashem has afflicted her" [Lamentations 1:5], and likewise throughout Lamentations with the Tetragrammaton (Havayah), showing that everything unfolds in...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Whoever is pristine and free from sins of passion requires extraordinary vigilance regarding anger and bloodshed to which he is susceptible; for as is known, "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" are two opposites, representing the right and left sides within evil and as I heard regarding Jeroboam son of Nebat who was called an Ephraimite (Efrati)—meaning he never experienced a nocturnal emission in his days, while his mother's name was Tzeruah (afflicted with tzara'at), showing his flaw lay in anger.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Deuteronomy, Nitzavim 3:2
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Means those possessing Chochma (wisdom) are placed in juxtaposition to the infants (also small children), for infant, taf in Hebrew, is connected to the word for “drop,” tipah in Hebrew, meaning that they possess only a small amount of consciousness (da’at, also “knowledge”). Then accordingly, when any mistake happens even to the youngest children, it affects even the heads, for the taf possessed a little consciousness from the head.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: I Samuel 1:19: ‘Early next morning they bowed low before GOD, and they went back home to Ramah. Elkanah knew his wife Hannah and GOD remembered her.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (I Samuel 1:19) to illuminate his exposition here (“And likewise regarding Hannah it is said: "and Hashem remembered her" [I Samuel 1:19] with the Tetragrammaton, yet her explicit personal name was omitted—unlike Rachel—phrased anonymously as "and He remembered her,"...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:13 (§4)
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And that is Amalek, the first of the nations, concerning whom it was commanded: "you shall blot out"; and therefore Esau is the root of destructive wrath, for on his account was the attribute of anger created in the world; wherefore the seed of Joseph and Rachel, who possess the trait of holy zeal, pour out their wrath upon the place fitting for wrath—upon Amalek.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 1:14–16
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Upon the arrival of the Seventh Day he must draw back, constricting his active drives so as to return all vitality to the Blessed Name, occupying himself with no voluntary mundane labors whatsoever, but cleaving solely unto Hashem, who is his primal Source and the realm whence he issued forth; as taught in the Holy Zohar (Beshalach 47b) explaining this verse: “He who invites a guest must attend solely to him and to no one else.”

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Genesis 19:17: ‘When they had brought them outside, one said, “Flee for your life! Do not look behind you, nor stop anywhere in the Plain; flee to the hills, lest you be swept away.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Genesis 19:17) to illuminate his exposition here (“And just as we find regarding the wicked—where Lot was commanded, "Look not behind you" [Genesis 19:17] because he was tainted like them— so it is regarding the righteous: when both are righteous and the Holy One...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: "And see the recompense of the wicked" Psalms 91:8—for it was said to Lot: "Look not al tabet behind you" Genesis 19:17, referring to one who is not spared by his own intrinsic merit, where gazing represents direct habatah; whereas the righteous man who is saved by his own merit stands far removed from the retribution of the wicked, viewing it passively from afar re'iyah, which is permitted—hence "you shall see tir'eh".
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Genesis, Lech Lecha 3
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: "And God said unto Avraham: And as for you, you shall keep My covenant, you, and your seed after you throughout their generations" (Genesis 17:9). The reason Avraham did not observe the mitzvah of circumcision before being commanded, whereas we find in the Gemara (Yoma 28b): 'Avraham our Father observed even Eruv Tavshilin'; is that indeed, all other commandments serve as a protective guard for man so that he walk in accordance with 'God made man upright' (Ecclesiastes 7:29), and not swerve to an extreme, but proceed along the balanced path; for if one becomes excessively immersed in a single pursuit, he will distort the straight path and stray from it…

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Exodus 12:22: ‘Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and apply some of the blood that is in the basin to the lintel and to the two doorposts. None of you shall go outside the door of your house until morning.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Exodus 12:22) to illuminate his exposition here (“And as is likewise written in Egypt: "and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning" [Exodus 12:22], because both these and those were idolaters; wherefore Hannah's name was not stated...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And as written in the Zohar Noach 63a regarding Noah and similarly Israel at the Exodus from Egypt: "Let none of you go out of the door of his house" Exodus 12:22, see there. And this is because there too the accusation arose: "these are idolaters and those are idolaters," meaning they had not achieved complete victory in the heart; for the heart, being the wellspring of life and living water, has no boundary, whereas that which is enclosed is bounded, for every fence has a defined perimeter.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Tiferet Yosef, Talmud Anthology, Berakhot 6
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Regarding the dispute in Berakhot 9a over eating the Paschal offering in haste (be-chipazon) until midnight versus until dawn: ‘the haste of Egypt’ signifies breaking free at once from the grip of material bondage, while ‘the haste of the Shekhinah’ signifies the swiftness of supernal illumination descending before the forces of judgment can impede it.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Ref: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Novellae, Rif, Berachot 1:3
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Folio 5a, s.v. Mipnei: "To be vigilant and flee from suspicion." – [Note]: See Shabbat [118b]: Rabbi Yose said: "May my portion be among those who are suspected unjustly of a wrong they did not commit... for they suspected me and I was innocent," which ostensibly requires study [against fleeing suspicion]. – And see further in Shabbat [149b]: Anyone on whose account his fellow is punished is not permitted to enter the partition of the Holy One; – and in Yoma [19b]: He who suspects the righteous is afflicted in his body.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Tetzaveh 3:6
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: It teaches man to guard himself and to see that because of him no damage is done to his fellow man. Then his peers will not be able to suspect him, and then be punished for suspecting him in vain. Then he too will be punished for causing his fellow man to be punished. “To do” teaches of reliance, and the point of reliance is the performance of mitzvot, such that a man can stand in prayer and support himself on them.This is as it is written (Tehilim, 104:3), “who makes the clouds His chariot,”

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Amos 5:15: ‘Hate evil and love good,And establish justice in the gate;Perhaps the ETERNAL, the God of Hosts,Will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Amos 5:15) to illuminate his exposition here (“making it accessible to all Jacob's descendants, who are designated collectively after the seed of Rachel, the mainstay of the house: "the remnant of Joseph" [Amos 5:15]. Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And every Jewish soul is incorporated of both, for both embrace the entire nation: for all Israel are designated upon the name of Yosef as "the remnant of Joseph" (Amos 5:15), and upon the name of Yehudah as "Jews" (Yehudim); and "Jews" is their primary title, because "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good and sins not" (Koheles 7:20); and from Yosef they are merely a "remnant," seeing that the bulk of his tribe assimilated and was lost in the exile of the Ten Tribes.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 52:1–3
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “And the whole earth was of one language and of one speech.” In Midrash Rabbah (38:4) and Tanchuma here: This is what Solomon said (Proverbs 27:22): “Though you bray a fool in a mortar among crushed grain with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.” So stood the Generation of Enosh, who called the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, upon idols, as it is said (Genesis 4:26): “Then began men to call upon the name of the Lord”; and the Holy One flooded a third of the world, as it is said (Amos 5:8): “He that calls for the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth, the Lord is His name.”

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Genesis 30:1: ‘When Rachel saw that she had borne Jacob no children, she became envious of her sister; and Rachel said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I shall die.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Genesis 30:1) to illuminate his exposition here (“Namely, when a person pleads simply for children for their own sake, seeking to be fruitful and multiply, as Rachel said: "and if not, I am dead" [Genesis 30:1], for one without children is considered as dead. And...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And Rachel “envied her sister” (Bereishis 30:1), ” — “and Rachel saw that she had borne Yaakov no children, and Rachel envied her sister, and said to Yaakov, ‘Give me children — and if not, I am as dead.’” R’ Tzadok’s use: envy is the very opposite of coveting, yet Rachel “envied” this coveting — desiring the dudaim, which in truth did not belong to her; this is “coveting what is not one’s own,” and it is precisely her rectification of it (ceding the tzaddik’s couch, a “good eye”) that is the subject of this se’if..
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:33–34
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: For the hope and longing for this salvation never truly ceased from you (and as explained in Parashat Vayeira on “And Sarah bore a son in his old age”). And even that which he said to Him (Genesis 17:18): “O that Yishmael might live before You!” corresponds to this commandment “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor”, for 'your neighbor' is the Holy One, as brought in the Zohar (Beshalach 55b); and Hashem had promised him: “And I will bless her, and give you a son also of her”.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Gittin 57b: ‘Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says, and some say that it was Rabbi Ami who says this, and some say that it was taught in a baraita: There was an incident involving four hundred boys and girls who were taken as captives for the purpose of prostitution. The oldest child among them expounded the verse: “The Lord said, I will bring back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea” (Psalms 68:23). “I will bring back from Bashan,” i.e., from between the teeth [bein shen] of the lion, and “I will bring…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Gittin 57b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this deep desire is characteristic of the Israelite, as I heard regarding the Talmudic statement (Gittin 57b): "The descendants of Haman studied Torah," which occurred because Saul spared Agag that night, as...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And they said [in the Mechilta] that “we do not accept converts from Amalek”; yet, nonetheless, “of the descendants of Haman, [some] taught children in Yerushalayim” (in Bnei Brak — Gittin 57b). And perforce this was because “a gentile of his descendants came upon a bas Yisrael” — [where] “the child is kosher and is a Jew,” yet is nonetheless also “called the son of the gentile,” as it says in the Torah, “and he was the son of an Egyptian man” (Vayikra 24:10), ” — “and the son of an Israelite woman went out — and he was the son of an Egyptian man — among the Children of Israel.”
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Pinchas 1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “Pinchas, son of Elazar, son of Aaron the Priest, has turned back My wrath from upon the children of Israel in his zealously avenging My zeal among them” (Numbers 25:11). Because Pinchas acted without any trace of personal anger or self-regard, purely out of burning love for the honor of Heaven and the survival of Israel, he was rewarded with the covenant of eternal peace.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 24: ('Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 24', 'https://www.sefaria.org/Tanna_DeBei_Eliyahu_Rabbah.24', '‘In the future judgment, even the very stone with which a transgressor was stoned and the tree upon which one was hanged are destined to give an accounting before the Holy One, blessed be He, so that every instrument through which strict judgment was enacted is purified and accounted for.’') Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 2, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 24) to illuminate his exposition here (“which occurred because Saul spared Agag that night, as related in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (ch. 24) that Agag grieved that his lineage not be extinguished, and in reward for this longing Haman descended from him;...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And for this one is punished even when it is for the sake of a mitzvah. And our Sages stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 24): even the stone with which one was stoned and the tree upon which one was hanged are destined to give reckoning. Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 20: ('Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 20', 'https://www.sefaria.org/Tanna_DeBei_Eliyahu_Rabbah.20', '‘Why did Ashur merit such greatness? Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And when the Blessed Name conceals His light Above for a moment, it appears throughout all worlds as though this person were completely righteous. And therefore they stated in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah (chapter 20): the reward of Ashur was that Sennacherib issued from him; and behold, Ashur was already in the World of Truth, so what reward to him was the worldly prosperity of Sennacherib, knowing there that this is vanity and falsehood?
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Deuteronomy, Ha'Azinu 4

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 4
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: In the vision of the burning bush—“the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed” (Exodus 3:2), and the Divine Name “I Shall Be As I Shall Be” (Exodus 3:14): the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to Moses that His Presence dwells within the lowliest thornbush of Israel’s affliction, accompanying them in this distress and in every future distress until their complete redemption.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Shemot Rabbah 3:8: ‘“Go and gather the elders of Israel, and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers, God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying: I have remembered you, and what is being done to you in Egypt” (Exodus 3:16). “Go and gather the elders of Israel.” The elders always uphold Israel, and thus it says: “And all Israel, and its elders, and its officers, and its judges, stood on this side and on that side of the ark” (Joshua 8:33). When is Israel capable of standing? It is when they have elders. Why, when the Temple was standing, did they consult with the elders, as it is stated: “Ask your father and he will tell you; your elders and they will say to you” (Deuteronomy…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Shemot Rabbah 3:8) to illuminate his exposition here (“And the Sages stated [Shemot Rabbah 3:8] that this sign was handed down in their tradition: whoever arrives with this wording is the true redeemer. And ostensibly, what kind of authenticating sign is this? Since it...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And the clarification was: immediately upon the arrival of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, "and the people believed" (Shemos 4:31). And it is known that everywhere the term "the people" (ha-am) denotes lowliness; and in the book Or Zarua (Hilchot Keriat Shema §7) he explains that in am ha'aretz, the word am is like the Aramaic amya, meaning dimness and the absence of light; and therefore Moshe Rabbeinu feared: "Behold, they will not believe me" (Shemos 4:1).
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 52:9
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: However, since Hashem established this mode of governance in this world by His sovereign will, so that in human perception it appears that agency is granted, this implies that this governance is likewise an authentic reality, His will constituting His glory; for this forms the entire foundation of this physical world, akin to what is taught in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 3:6): Do you ask concerning My Name? According to My operational attribute am I designated.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Psalms 121:5: ‘GOD is your guardian, GOD is your protectionat your right hand.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Psalms 121:5) to illuminate his exposition here (“But in truth it is known from our Sages on "Hashem is your shadow" [Psalms 121:5], that He acts like a shadow reflecting whatever the body does, all His attributes operating measure for measure, not arbitrarily, but...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And through wasted seed divine influx is channeled from Yesod into external husks rather than Malchut. Man acting as a supernal mirror ("Hashem is your shadow" [Psalms 121:5]), human actions reflecting above, which constitutes taking nine Sefirot without Malchut.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 42:1–4
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “Every moving thing that lives shall be meat for you.” Concerning why meat was permitted to Noah and not to Adam; commentators (Ramban) reasoning it was because they were saved through him—yet why were fish permitted, when they were not saved by the Ark? Rather, Hashem does no injustice to any creature, all being created with their consent (Rosh Hashanah 11a).

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Zechariah 1:3: ‘Say to them further:Thus said GOD of Hosts: Turn back to me—says GOD of Hosts—and I will turn back to you—said GOD of Hosts.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Zechariah 1:3) to illuminate his exposition here (“only that the Blessed Name desires the lower awakening (itaruta d'letata) to precede: "Return unto Me, and I will return unto you" [Zechariah 1:3], while we plead: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall be turned"...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Ref: Likkutei Maamarim, On Book of Joshua:23 (§2)
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And this is Hashem's call: "Return unto Me" Zechariah 1:3—mastering Torah after the concealment of divine providence; and when he repents and God returns to him affirming human agency, the stumbling is dissolved in retrospective truth. And this is why Hashem is titled "abundant in pardon," forgiveness issuing from His side; while from man's perspective one must feel brokenness: "and my sin is ever before me" Psalms 51:5, confessing sins on successive Yom Kippurs (Yoma 86b).
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Yitro 7:8
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: The reason the mitzvot signifying action precede the mitzvot signifying will is that if one sins in action, God forbid, he will go back and ponder it and find some thought to hold responsible for it, meaning in the very source of his life. So then he must “do teshuva” [return to the way of God] in this regard, sincerely mending his ways and thus healing his roots.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Lamentations 5:21: ‘Take us back, O ETERNAL One, to Yourself,And let us come back;Renew our days as of old!’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Lamentations 5:21) to illuminate his exposition here (“only that the Blessed Name desires the lower awakening (itaruta d'letata) to precede: "Return unto Me, and I will return unto you" [Zechariah 1:3], while we plead: "Turn us unto You, Hashem, and we shall be turned"...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: As is known, “as water [reflects] a face,” and the arousal from below and from Above rouse one another; only that we say “draw me [after You we will run]” and “return us,” that the arousal from Above precede to rouse us, and we will be drawn and run after Him. But Hashem says the reverse, “Return to Me [and I will return to you],” and upon this hangs the whole length of the exile — for Hashem wills that we arouse, with an arousal from below, and “if Israel do teshuvah they are immediately redeemed.”
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Tetzaveh 1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “And you will command the children of Israel … take unto yourself pure olive oil ….” (Shemot, 27:20)“Unto yourself,” meaning to the Chochma (wisdom) inherent in every soul of Israel, and all the wisdom of Israel is called in the name of Moshe Rabeynu. To this God commanded that every one of Israel shall take to the wisdom inside of him some pure olive oil, meaning refined wisdom, and that is that he should not turn to any side that might be tainted.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Exodus 3:18: ‘They will listen to you; then you shall go with the elders of Israel to the king of Egypt and you shall say to him, ‘The ETERNAL, the God of the Hebrews, became manifest to us. Now therefore, let us go a distance of three days into the wilderness to sacrifice to the ETERNAL our God.’’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Exodus 3:18) to illuminate his exposition here (“and so it was in Egypt through an awakening from Above, the Blessed Name sending them "I have surely visited," and through this "they shall hearken to your voice" [Exodus 3:18], immediately believing this speech....”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 10:7 (§14)
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And this is the mystery of "Let us go... and sacrifice"— that we become intimately near to Hashem and exit the legal status of converts, which constitutes the entire purpose of the Exodus from Egypt, which is the elevation from the designation of 'strangers' to the title of 'Israel.' And this was an eternal redemption, such that they are no longer slaves to Pharaoh, for from that moment onward no Jew is ever a wandering alien again, which is what was termed being 'Pharaoh's slaves.'
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 35:1
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “That you may remember the day of your going forth from the land of Egypt all the days of your life” (Deuteronomy 16:3): the initial illumination given at the Exodus was an awakening from Above in haste (be-chipazon), and our lifelong task through the days and nights of this world is to internalize that sudden flash of freedom until it becomes the steady, conscious possession of our hearts.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Exodus 4:31: ‘and the assembly was convinced. When they heard that GOD had taken note of the Israelites and had seen their plight, they bowed low in homage.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Exodus 4:31) to illuminate his exposition here (“And so it was: "And the people believed; and when they heard that Hashem had visited..." [Exodus 4:31], through hearing that He visited, faith entered their hearts. But Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: That even those submerged in the deepest immersion in the mundane affairs of this world possess an inner root cleaved unto the Blessed Name; and this is the root of faith, they being "believers, the children of believers" (Shabbat 97a); and immediately when Moshe Rabbeinu came and aroused them, "and the people believed" (Shemos 4:31) immediately in the Blessed Name; and in the merit of faith they were redeemed (Mechilta, Beshalach 6); meaning that through this the light awakened little by little within their hearts, until they merited to emerge from darkness into great light.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 48:29–31
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: As in the Zohar (Behar 111b): In two manners are Israel designated before the Holy One: they are called servants, as written: “for they are My servants”; and they are called children, as written: “You are the children of the Lord your God”; and even though called a son (“Israel is My son, My firstborn”), he must never remove himself from the category of servant to serve his Father in all services that constitute his Father's glory; a son cleaves perpetually to his father without any separation, none protesting; while a servant executes the labor of his master, rectifying the order of the world.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Exodus 4:1: ‘But Moses spoke up and said, “What if they do not believe me and do not listen to me, but say: GOD did not appear to you?”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Exodus 4:1) to illuminate his exposition here (“wherefore he said: "behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice" [Exodus 4:1]—"me" and "my voice" specifically, not deeming himself worthy or that his personal voice had power to be heard. And this...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Ref: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 7:15
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And as I wrote above, Moses stumbled in uttering "behold, they will not believe me" [Exodus 4:1], being afflicted with leprosy (Shabbat 97a), wherefore he fled into exile, exile effecting atonement (Makkot 2b) [and so all of Israel's exiles serve to purge slander, heralding Mashiach who embodies the healing of the tongue], like an accidental killer fleeing to a city of refuge, slander mirroring homicide.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Noach 20:10–11
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: As in Isaiah 6:3: “And one called unto another,” rendered: “and they receive one from another,” each receiving from above and bestowing below. And as in Zohar Shemot (4a): Though he is a supernal king he is feminine relative to the hidden point above, and masculine relative to the king below, all unfolding in this manner.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Exodus 4:10: ‘But Moses said to GOD, “Please, O my Sovereign, I have never been a man of words, either in times past or now that You have spoken to Your servant; I am slow of speech and slow of tongue.”’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 3, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Exodus 4:10) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this explains his subsequent protest: "I am not a man of words" [Exodus 4:10], meaning: my words lack the power to penetrate the listener's heart to effect transformation; for a "man of words" is one whose speech...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Only because he initially experienced an impediment in speech—"I am not a man of words... but am slow of speech" (Exodus 4:10)—which is the earthly dimension of speech outside his elevated rung; and Hashem aids only those who experience deficiency and need salvation, as Moses challenged the ministering angels: "Does an evil inclination exist among you?" (Shabbat 89a), showing that perfect beings do not receive the Torah.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Ki Tisa 11
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “Carve for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke” (Exodus 34:1)—on which the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses, ‘May your strength be firm (yishar kochacha) for breaking them!’ (Shabbat 87a). Through the shattering of the first tablets was born the power of the Oral Torah and the capacity of ba’alei teshuvah to renew holiness from below.
